rule: Read a file once: validate and display the same text (`schema.check_text`). Never validate, then read again to show.
Keep an invalid record visible and marked, but pass it through `schema.strip_invalid` first so no wrongly typed field reaches code that reads it.

No check may raise on any input: wrong types, null, NaN/Infinity, raw non-object lines, nesting 50,000 deep. Any exception becomes one error for that record. Test it with a property test over every field, not with one example.
Cross-record checks (hooks) run only on records with valid shape.
Never change a test's input to make it pass; fix the code. Commit the checks before the code.
One rule in one place beats a reminder in every step: e.g. one "run schema.py check after every write" sentence at each entry point.
A schema that accepts a value the reader or renderer crashes on is a bug in the schema: test that every accepted example renders.
A missing value is null; optional fields accept null as absent, consistently.

Shared files (schema.py, page.*, base/conversation/spec schemas, tests/page.test.js) are edited by several tasks: keep edits local to your function, copy shared files to all skills, and expect a merge; never rename or re-declare a helper another task may also add.
When a verifier confirms a finding with a script or input, turn it into a repo test in the fix's round.
